standard.title: First Nations dance and culture
standard.description: explore the ways that First Nations Australians use dance to continue and revitalise cultures
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explore how First Nations Australians use dance to communicate connection to and responsibility for Country/Place (Y3-4). They can identify element use in First Nations dance and understand the cultural purposes of specific dance occasions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore the ways that First Nations Australians use dance to continue and revitalise cultures.

nodes.label: Dance as cultural continuation and revitalisation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain why cultural expressions including dance are critical for sharing, continuing and revitalising First Nations Australian cultures.
nodes.minimum_width: Describing at least one way that dance helps First Nations Australians continue or revitalise a cultural practice — using a specific example.
nodes.typical_width: Exploring, using resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians, how and why cultural expressions are critical for sharing, continuing and revitalising cultures; investigating how meaning and purpose are communicated in dance at community events; experiencing how First Nations Australians' stories and ideas communicate connection to and responsibility for Country/Place.
wider: Explore how narrative dances maintain culture — examining specific examples of dances that communicate knowledge about sustainable approaches or place-naming stories
Investigate how community events use dance to communicate cultural knowledge to the broader community — noting what knowledge is shared and with whom
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding dance as a vehicle for cultural continuation and revitalisation — not merely performance — is the conceptual shift required for meaningful engagement with the more complex issues of cultural diversity, ICIP rights and identity in Y7-8.

response_modes.reason: Revitalisation is a concept that requires contextualisation — students need to understand what cultural continuity means and why it matters before they can appreciate dance's role. Use resources created by First Nations Australians and guided discussion to build this understanding.

success_criteria: Student can explain what it means for First Nations Australians to use dance to continue or revitalise their culture
Student can describe at least one specific example of dance serving this purpose

nodes.label: Investigating meaning and purpose in First Nations dance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate how meaning and purpose are communicated in specific First Nations Australian dance works — using Viewpoints questions to deepen inquiry.
nodes.minimum_width: Observing one First Nations Australian dance work and using at least two Viewpoints questions to investigate how meaning is communicated.
nodes.typical_width: Investigating how meaning and purpose are communicated in dances performed at community events or via resources created/co-created by First Nations Australians; using Viewpoints questions to build understanding ('What do I already know?', 'What do I need to learn?', 'What questions would I ask the dancers?'); exploring how dances communicate sustainable practices for caring for land, sea, sky.
wider: Compare how two different First Nations Australian dance practices communicate cultural knowledge — noting what is shared versus what is community-specific
Develop and pursue an inquiry question about a First Nations Australian dance practice — following protocols and using resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians

response_modes.reason: Students' capacity to investigate First Nations dance meaningfully deepens with exposure to multiple examples from diverse communities. Breadth here prevents reductive single-example conclusions.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who investigate meaning and purpose across multiple First Nations Australian dance examples develop genuine inquiry skills and cross-cultural literacy — preparation for the analytical and ethical demands of Y7-8.
success_criteria: Student uses Viewpoints questions to investigate how meaning is communicated in a First Nations Australian dance
Student can explain what the dance communicates about culture, knowledge or connection to Country/Place
